title: What the prescription itself must contain under the format regulation
rule_summary: 105 CMR 721.020(C) requires the practitioner's NAME AND ADDRESS to be clearly indicated on the Prescription, and a hospital or clinic Prescription to carry the name and address of the hospital or clinic. 105 CMR 721.020(D) requires the Prescription to contain: (1) the REGISTRATION NUMBER of the practitioner; (2) the DATE OF ISSUANCE; (3) the name, dosage and strength per dosage unit of the controlled substance prescribed, AND THE QUANTITY OF DOSAGE UNITS; (4) the NAME AND ADDRESS OF THE PATIENT, except in a veterinary Prescription, a Prescription for naloxone or another opioid antagonist approved by the Department, or a Prescription issued under 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7) or (A)(12), in which case the name and address may be left blank, and where the person taking delivery of a naloxone or other approved opioid antagonist Prescription MAY, but is not required to, be used in place of the patient's name; (5) DIRECTIONS FOR USE, including any required cautionary statements; (6) a STATEMENT INDICATING THE NUMBER OF TIMES TO BE REFILLED; and (7) for an OPIOID substance in schedule II, a NOTATION THAT THE PATIENT MAY FILL THE PRESCRIPTION, UPON REQUEST, IN AN AMOUNT LESS THAN the recommended full quantity indicated. Under 105 CMR 721.020(E) a Prescription issued by a certified nurse practitioner, psychiatric nurse mental health clinical specialist or certified registered nurse anesthetist must also contain the NAME OF THE SUPERVISING qualified healthcare professional, unless that nurse is authorized for independent practice under 244 CMR.
exam_relevance: Tests the content of the prescription as the regulation states it, which is broader than the statutory element list: the quantity of dosage units, the refill statement, the supervising-professional name, and a patient name-and-address exception with four limbs rather than one.
exceptions: The patient name and address may be left blank on a veterinary prescription, a naloxone or other Department-approved opioid antagonist prescription, or a prescription issued under 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7) or (A)(12).
The supervising-professional name is not required where the issuing nurse is authorized for independent practice under 244 CMR.
common_confusions: Treating the statutory element list in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 22(a) as the complete set of required content, when the regulation adds the quantity of dosage units, the refill statement and the supervising-professional name.
Naming the veterinary prescription as the only exception to the patient name and address requirement.
Missing that the schedule II opioid partial-fill notation is required on the prescription by the regulation as well as by statute.
verification_notes: 105 CMR 721.020(C), (D)(1)-(7) and (E) read verbatim from the official publication dated 9/27/24 on 2026-09-10. Added because the GPT-FRESH-B4-SG-REPAIR-V6B audit found SG-MA-SCHEDULE-VI presenting the s. 22(a) statutory elements as a closed list, and no canonical rule carried 105 CMR 721.020(C)-(E) at all, so the missing content could not be taught anywhere. Independent audit still required.
